method: Independent current-snapshot audit after reading AGENTS.md. Read all assigned deployment modules, tests, CI, scripts, configuration, prose and ordinary feature evidence; traced authority, mutation, recovery and resource lifetimes through complete code paths. Parsed every lockfile line and recursively verified all capability inventory entries, exact protocol/schema/group closure and referenced file hashes, then reviewed every unique group and workflow assessment. Historical linked report files were checked only as opaque bytes for existence/hash and were not read for conclusions. Executed only four justified portable test files through the targeted runner. Rechecked every assigned file hash and the full source snapshot before reporting.

validations.name: assignment-and-snapshot
validations.detail: Baseline and final current snapshot match. AGENTS and the assignment were read before the first recorded audit baseline. No source, test, documentation or ordinary feature-evidence edits were made.

validations.name: privilege-and-process-boundaries
validations.detail: Reviewed distinct gateway/control/native/build identities, exact sudo verbs, fixed launchers, root-owned code and unit recognition, group separation, cgroup stop evidence, subreaper cleanup, no_new_privs, descriptor closure, resource limits, host-policy oneshot and immutable provider bind generations. Test substitutions and actual-identity Linux fixtures were distinguished.

validations.name: build-and-archive-publication
validations.detail: Traced pinned distributions and integrity checks; sanitized registry-only dependency input; separate network fetch and offline candidate stages; private bounded loop filesystems; producer-stop-gated descriptor imports; physical archive headers, PAX/GNU metadata, implicit-directory reservations, XZ memory and file/tree budgets; complete runtime manifests, exact release reuse and pointer/journal recovery. Candidate marker files do not independently authorize publication.

validations.name: management-provider-tls-recovery
validations.detail: Traced request admission, durable receipt identity/digests, spool reservations and locks, disconnected waiters, confirmed unit/cgroup cleanup and preserved unknowns. Reviewed provider revisions, endpoint-scoped key reuse, gateway credential confirmation, Bedrock token delivery, complete provider requirements, host drift checks, trusted control update/rollback barriers and retained old/candidate generations. HTTPS identity/database/key pairing, immutable certificate generations, exact host/port reuse, unconditional forward_auth, independent gateway token, original active/enabled restoration and explicit stop-confirmed repair were traced.

validations.name: workspace-git-worktree-flows
validations.detail: Read all workspace helpers and assigned tests: descriptor-bound roots and protected paths; file revision CAS/no-replace publication; recovery retention and explicit destinations; Git clean view, disabled hooks/filters/network, copied index, prepared update-ref transaction and original-index preservation; index recovery leases; supervisor-bound linked-worktree identities, raw object materialization and whole-checkout archive/restore retaining dirty/staged/untracked/ignored data. Native-owned recovery records were not treated as positive gateway proof.

validations.name: release-ci-and-test-validity
validations.detail: Reviewed affected-test mapping including deleted/shared/platform inputs, ordinary versus root fixtures, hosted Linux root job restrictions, pinned actions and native version inputs, targeted zero-selection/skip rejection, unchanged three-round full-suite gate, exhaustive audit coverage union, snapshot exclusions and release scanner byte/history handling. Read all assigned test bodies, setup, failure injection and platform skips; no full deployment suite or release-wide suite was executed.

validations.name: portable-targeted-tests
validations.command: HARNESS_TEST_PYTHON=<PYTHON_RUNTIME> node scripts/run-tests.mjs --targeted tests/deploy/test_dependency_lock.py tests/deploy/test_request_spool.py tests/deploy/test_journal_schema.py tests/deploy/test_origins.py
validations.rationale: Small portable checks for bounded/stable lock reads, spool admission/lifetime/unknown receipts using substituted system operations, current journal schema and canonical origin validation. These do not claim real root or systemd execution.

validations.name: complete-lock-inventory
validations.detail: Independent constrained structural parser consumed every line with duplicate-key/indentation/unsupported-scalar rejection. All root specifiers match package.json; only one importer; exact workspace overrides; all resolutions contain SHA-512 integrity with valid 64-byte digests; every dependency resolves; all snapshots/packages are reachable. Reviewed all distinct engine ranges, platform/peer metadata, executable package inventory and pinned vision SDK/Zod resolution. This is structural integrity/compatibility review, not a live registry or advisory recheck.

validations.name: complete-capability-inventory
validations.detail: Strict JSON duplicate-key parse; exact typed-method set, actual parameter declarations/imports including optional and parameterless forms, JSON oneOf method pointers, stable/experimental membership, one-to-one group membership, statuses/classification count closure, and all paths/hashes/line bounds checked. All 50 unique group assessments and 15 additional workflow assessments were read; every method assessment exactly matches its reviewed group. No capability file was regenerated.

validations.name: ordinary-feature-evidence-and-provenance
validations.detail: Read each ordinary evidence JSON, preserving its failed attempts, platform skips, mock/native/external distinctions and sourceFrozen/fullSuiteRun disclaimers. All locally specified file/report references exist; historical report bytes were hashed without parsing their conclusions. The 29 differences are older source/test hashes explicitly captured at writing, not claims of retested current bytes. The current capability inventory has no such differences. Both provenance bundle hashes and generation counts match; timeline embedded TypeScript matches current bytes, and its generatedSha256 matches protocol/json/v2/ThreadTimelineListResponse.json.

validations.name: checker-setup-and-corrections
validations.detail: Initial dependency discovery found no directly resolvable yaml/js-yaml/pnpm-lock parser and Python had no yaml module; no dependencies were installed. A temporary independent checker first failed on a reserved Python keyword, then on its own overly narrow parameter-source/optional-parameter assumptions; three assertion-failing iterations were corrected against current generated imports/types. A preliminary path classifier included HTTP request paths; those observations were explicitly separated from filesystem references. An attempted hash of nonexistent protocol/json/v2/ThreadTimelineEntry.json failed; filename inventory and opaque generated-file hashes located the exact recorded ThreadTimelineListResponse.json instead. These were checker/setup errors, not product test failures. The final exhaustive checks completed successfully.

validations.name: inspection-output-completeness
validations.detail: Overlong initial combined output was not counted as full inspection. Affected source/document ranges were reread in bounded complete chunks. The two large inventories used exhaustive structured checks plus semantic review rather than truncated terminal output.

validations.name: prohibited-and-platform-execution
validations.detail: No SSH, online service mutation, full suite, root deployment execution, model inference, external MCP, external provider validation or personal credentials. Linux-only root/systemd/cgroup/reboot, live TLS/Authelia, sandbox mounts and cross-UID behavior were reviewed in source/tests and existing ordinary evidence only, not re-executed this round.

limitations: This complete result covers independent inspection of the 115 assigned files on the named snapshot. It does not certify every external service, host kernel or production deployment behavior.

Only 28 tests in four portable files ran in this round, with zero failures and zero skips. Linux root fixtures, real systemd boot/condition/cgroup behavior, namespace and loop-mount enforcement, native cross-UID integrations, actual TLS trust/login and restart-after-power-loss remain unexecuted here.

HTTPS hard interruption during multi-file publication can require explicit repair; automatic reboot atomicity was not established. Tracing did not establish an authentication bypass, wrong identity/key binding, lost journal or unsafe explicit repair from that scenario, so it is not reported as an actionable defect.

Ordinary historical feature evidence is limited to its original time-point source identity, substitutions, failures and skips. In particular, 29 older source/test hash observations differ from current files. Existing reports were never reused as independent audit conclusions.

Registry/advisory freshness, real ChatGPT/provider/cloud/OAuth/email/voice/AWS behavior and external MCP were not rechecked. Embedded version/integrity pins were reviewed locally without network execution.

Some narrative remote fixture paths and unlabeled standalone historical hashes have no locally specified target; they are contextual provenance, not newly verified live results. Locally explicit file/hash references were checked exhaustively.
